Definition: properly, to glitter from afar, i.e. to be eminent (as a superintendent, especially of the Temple services and its music); to be permanent
BiblicalUsage: The word names the one who leads the music, setting the singers in order with their harps, and the one set over the work of the temple, directing the labourers. It is the chief singer's mark on the psalm, and the overseer's place over Solomon's builders.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God puts overseers over both song and stone: the music must be led and the work must be watched, and the same word covers them both because both are His service. The chief singer and the overseer answer to the same Lord, and neither task is beneath His notice.
RelatedPeople: King David; King Solomon; Ezra; Habakkuk
